note: Waivers for scripts/check-i18n-en-drift.mjs (objectui#3650): an en string changed and one
or more of the nine translation packs deliberately did not follow it.
Shape:  "<dotted key>": { "en": "<the NEW en text, verbatim>", "reason": "…", "issue": "objectstack#1234" } (objectui#1234 for entries that predate the ui tree's move into this repo)
This file ships EMPTY and holds no backlog, unlike scripts/i18n-call-site-key-baseline.json.
That gate measures a STATE (keys missing from en today), so it could inventory the debt. This
one judges an EVENT in a diff (en changed, the packs did not), and 'is ja's sentence still
what en's now means?' is the semantic question no gate can answer -- objectui#3625 was eight
idiomatic, native-script, mutually distinct translations of a retired sentence, green under
every mechanical judgement there is. So there is nothing to write down here at landing.
An entry must transcribe the new en text, which is what makes it reviewable and what makes it
expire: the gate re-checks that text against the en pack on every run, so the waiver covers
that one sentence and stops applying the moment the key changes again. A waiver that fires
nothing is fine (every run after its PR merges sees an empty diff); a waiver whose text is
gone fails the build until it is deleted or renewed.
Adding an entry also means raising WAIVER_CEILING in scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-en-drift.test.ts.
That is the ratchet: the ceiling is free to fall and costs a reviewed test edit to rise.
The first five entries below are objectui#3878's ellipsis convergence, and they are the one shape
this ledger was designed for: en moved to U+2026 on keys where the packs ALREADY spelled it
U+2026, so there is nothing for them to follow. That is the inverse of the usual drift -- here
en was the outlier, not the packs -- and the transcribed sentences below are the evidence, since
the gate re-checks each one against en on every run. Four of the five had all nine packs already
correct; search.placeholder had zh already correct and the other eight followed in that same PR.
The sixth, marketplace.searchPlaceholder (objectui#10969), has that search.placeholder shape: en
dropped the 'manifest ID' jargon, eight packs followed, and zh had already dropped it.
designerWaivers is the SECOND section, for the metadata-admin designer table population added by
objectui#8834 (packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts). Same shape, same expiry rule,
same ceiling discipline -- separate map because each section is validated against the en values of
its own population, and a designer key is not a pack key. Keys are prefixed with their table, e.g.
"ENGINE_STRINGS.engine.directory.title". It ships EMPTY and holds no backlog either.
Its first seven entries (objectstack#29729) are the one-word-per-state convergence in Studio's
flow run status: en moved Off/Disabled to 'Switched off' and On/Enabled to 'Switched on', the
word the landing, the ledger switch and the Setup page already used. zh already read 已停用 /
已启用 for every one of them, so there was nothing for it to follow.
